claim_results.reason: The 24 theorem statements, 10 definitions, two supporting recursion definitions and supplied readback agree with the local contract. Structured expression inspection confirms the quantified domains, implicit and explicit binders, signs and arithmetic types. The recurrence includes u(0)=0 and u(1)=1; existence and uniqueness require c≠0. The definitions themselves permit zero denominators through total real division. The scalar decomposition retains B/c*(v-w); its lower bound uses c>0, B≥0 and w≤v, and equality is equivalent to B=0 or v=w under the recurrence equation and c≠0. The recurrence induction uses coefficient assumptions at every k≥2. Products run over the inclusive natural interval [2,n], are empty at n=0,1, and comparisons with u require n≥1. Equality for B=0 does not impose positivity. The fixed example has solution 2^n-1, product 1 and strict inequality at every n+2; the negated equality theorem concerns these fixed coefficients only. The perturbed difference has the corrected delta coefficient and the stated exact values. All P2 parameters are real, all displayed denominator conditions are retained, and shifted denominators are covered. The complement theorem correctly permits m=3 and m=1/2. Independent exact polynomial calculations confirm the rational identities and specified values under their denominator hypotheses. No analytic identification or universal classification is inferred.

All 18 input hashes match. Parsing declarations.json confirms exactly 34 distinct targets. Its data reproduce both statement files exactly, and its ten explicit definition bodies match the definition closure. Traversal of all 8,032 dependency records finds no missing references, unknown declaration kinds or unsafe flags; every target reaches exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, agreeing with the supplied compiler axiom output. The author and replay build records consistently bind the supplied source and pins, report exit code 0, and record the same object hash. The inspection stdout hash and readback receipt hash also match. However, the negative-control sources and their source-bound execution records are absent: the supplied outputs establish recorded failures at an unsolved False goal, but cannot establish which assertions were tested. In addition, replay export equality is supported only by the hashes and assertions in RESULT.json; the replay export invocation and transcript are absent. These gaps prevent full approval of the requested machine-evidence obligation, despite the internal consistency of the supplied records.

limitations: No Lean compiler invocation, kernel recheck or negative-control rerun was performed. Compiler binaries, compiled objects and imported dependency artifacts are outside the supplied inputs and were not accessed.

Dependency closure was checked within the structured export. The export supplies theorem dependency lists but no theorem proof-expression bodies, so completeness of those lists could not be independently recomputed from proof terms.

The environment pins specify Lean v4.31.0 and mathlib revision fabf563a7c95a166b8d7b6efca11c8b4dc9d911f. Correspondence between those pins and the dependencies actually loaded in the recorded executions was not independently verified.

The supplied readback was independently compared with the declarations and contract. Its receipt matches the report hash, but its referenced dispatch and completion artifacts were not supplied, so generation provenance and blindness were not independently authenticated.

No legacy module or Mathlib dependency was rebuilt. Integration, analytic completeness, integral interpretations, asymptotics, operator-domain membership and spectral or quotient results remain outside this review.
Only the frozen packet and its listed snapshots were inspected. No source-project files were modified.
